newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: IBM joins LG to make computers in Korea.
newsitem.headline: IBM joins LG to make computers in Korea.

text.p: IBM Korea will team up with LG Electronics in a $30 million venture to manufacture and sell personal computers (PC) in South Korea, company officials and industry sources said on Monday.
Industry analysts said a combination of IBM's design and technology strengths and LG's vast sales network would create new opportunities for both players in a market enjoying double-digit growth.
LG Electronics is South Korea's third largest PC maker. It is a unit of the LG Group, the country's biggest home appliance manufacturer.
IBM Korea, a wholly-owned unit of the U.S. International Business Machine Corp. now sells imported PCs, but sales have been sluggish, partly because of high prices, analysts said.
LG-IBM Co will be capitalised at 24 billion won ($30 million), an industry source told Reuters. IBM Korea would hold a 51 percent stake and LG Electronics the rest.
Initially, the joint venture will utilise existing LG production lines to make PCs, the source said. Later, it will make IBM computers on its own lines.
LG will continue to make its own PC brands for the export market and hand over its domestic operations to the IBM joint venture, the source said.
Spokesmen for both companies confirmed the deal would go ahead, but declined to give details before a formal announcement is made on Tuesday.
"We aim to become the nation's number one PC maker," said an LG official, who declined to be named.

"It will give LG a chance to improve its brand recognition," said Woo Young-moo of Daewoo Securities. "Easier access to IBM's design and technology is the strongest point of the deal in favour of LG."
"IBM products are high-end goods so their sales are very sluggish in the Korean market," said Jon Chong-hwa of Hanuri Salomon Securities.
An IBM Korea official declined to give sales figures, saying only they were "very small".
Samsung Electronics now dominates PC sales in South Korea with a 30 percent market share followed by Trigem Computer with 15 percent, according to Hanuri Salomon figures.
LG Electronics claims a 10-14 percent market share with sales of 160,000 PCs in the first eight months of this year, up sharply from 100,000 units a year earlier.

Rhee Namuh, head of research of Dongbang Peregrine Securities, forecast domestic PC sales of two million units this year, up from 1.64 million last year, and predicted double-digit growth for the next several years.
"LG could not have survived if it insisted on doing PC business alone," he said.
